result.title: Does Learning Recurrent Networks Matter in Partially Observable RL?
result.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) under partial observability typically re- lies on recurrent networks to encode temporal information, with the recurrent module trained jointly with the policy or value function. This raises a natural question: is learning the recurrent network actually necessary? In this paper, we investigate whether a frozen recurrent network can provide sufficient memory for solving par- tially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs). Motivated by the theoretical foundations of Reservoir Computing (RC) and Generalized Reservoir Computing (GRC), we study a simple archi- tecture that combines a fixed recurrent network with a trainable nonlinear output module. We evaluate this approach across tasks with varying memory demands, observation modalities, and action spaces. Surprisingly, frozen recurrent networks support recall over hundreds of steps and achieve competitive control performance across diverse POMDPs, while using less than half the number of trainable parameters required by their fully trainable counterparts. These results suggest that learning the recurrent memory module is not always necessary for solving POMDPs. Frozen recurrent networks therefore provide a simple, parameter-efficient, and sur- prisingly strong baseline for partially observable RL. Our source code is available at https://github.com/Aphlios/FRN-POMDP

AI.brief_summary: 论文在部分可观测强化学习（POMDP）中追问「是否有必要训练循环网络」，提出将冻结的循环网络与可训练非线性输出模块组合，在多种记忆需求、观测模态和动作空间的任务上评估其记忆能力与控制性能，发现冻结循环网络可支持数百步回忆，并以不到一半的可训练参数取得有竞争力的表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「固定循环状态转移＋仅训练读出模块」的架构可为 LVR 中 latent 循环状态是否需要训练、状态更新与读出监督如何分工提供可核查的方法线索，但与视觉多模态推理并无直接实验关联。
